a90ac4e3c02a1ea796f99068f59350546a1537eb.summary: ANY.RUN reports a large-scale Magecart-style campaign active for at least 24 months, supported by over 100 domains. Its payment-skimming code hijacks checkout steps, imitates payment pages (notably Redsys in Spain), and sends card data over WebSocket. Victims are mostly retail e-commerce sites, but the report says banks bear the primary impact. Victims are in at least 12 countries, concentrated in Spain, France and the United States. The same injected code was also used to push an Android APK.

a90d655dfa8d409ccfc8e2c6a90466346e877b9b.summary: The Hacker News article (May 2017) reports that Russian authorities, working with Group-IB, arrested members of the Cron gang. The gang used the CronBot Android banking trojan, spread through fake bank and other apps, to intercept bank confirmation SMS codes and steal money. The article cites Group-IB and the Interior Ministry for a total of about 50 million rubles (nearly $900,000) taken from more than one million victims. The gang had also rented the Tiny.z malware and built web injections for French banks before the arrests.
